description: We are Team AIdınlık, passionate about space exploration, AI, and human health! We are building an AI-powered health monitoring system designed to safeguard astronauts during space missions. Our team brings core expertise in software engineering, data analysis, UI/UX design, and biomedical technologies to solve real-world space challenges.
summary: Baseline is an offline-capable crew health self-monitoring dashboard for long-duration missions, where ground support can be minutes away (Mars: 3–22 min one-way). Instead of fixed thresholds, it learns each astronaut's personal baseline from their first measurements and warns when values drift or trends worsen, even while still in the "normal" range (for example, falling sleep + rising pulse + lower mood = fatigue/stress pattern). It tracks nine indicators mapped to NASA HRP's five hazards, shows status on an interactive 3D body model using color, icon and text, offers step-by-step measurement guides and reminders, and generates a flight-surgeon report queued for delayed transmission. It does not diagnose; it supports decisions when Earth cannot answer in real time.
details:
What it does: Crew members log daily vitals (pulse, blood pressure, glucose, body temperature, radiation dose, exercise, sleep, mood). Baseline computes a personal baseline x₀ (the mean of the first 5 logs) and the deviation of each new reading xₙ from it:

Δ% = (xₙ − x₀) / x₀ × 100

where x₀ is the personal baseline and xₙ is the latest measurement. A least-squares line fitted to the last 6 logs gives the trend; when the trend or Δ% crosses a limit, the app raises early warnings and pattern alerts (fatigue/stress, cardiovascular adaptation, deconditioning), even when values are inside general ranges.

Benefits and expected impact: On Mars missions, ground support is delayed and crews must self-assess. Baseline gives personalized, actionable guidance, step-by-step measurement guides, daily reminders, and a flight-surgeon report that is queued and forwarded when the link allows. It works offline as a PWA.

Hazard mapping: Every indicator links to NASA HRP's five hazards (space radiation, isolation and confinement, distance from Earth, gravity fields, hostile/closed environments) and cites the matching HRP risk page.

Tools and technologies: HTML, CSS, JavaScript; three.js (3D anatomical model); SVG/Canvas charts; Service Worker and localStorage for offline use. Camera pulse estimation uses fingertip photoplethysmography (an estimate, not a medical device).

Creativity and design decisions: A personal baseline instead of one-size-fits-all limits; trend-based early warning; status always shown with color, icon and text (color-blind friendly); English interface with a Turkish option; guided tour; lite mode for low-power hardware.

Limitations: Baseline does not diagnose. Numeric normal ranges are general adult clinical references, not NASA medical standards, and should be replaced by flight-surgeon protocols.

Use of SI: The application code (HTML/CSS/JavaScript, 3D model, analysis logic, service worker), the documentation, the interface text and its English/Turkish translation, and the presentation were produced with the assistance of Claude (Anthropic) under the team's direction, then reviewed and tested by the team. No NASA logos, flags or mission identifiers are used.
